arxiv-2210-11341.title: SS-VAERR: Self-Supervised Apparent Emotional Reaction Recognition from Video
arxiv-2210-11341.creator: Marija Jegorova, Stavros Petridis, and Maja Pantic Meta Reality Labs, London, United Kingdom Department of Computing, Imperial College London, United Kingdom
arxiv-2210-11341.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marija Jegorova, Stavros Petridis, and Maja Pantic Meta Reality Labs, London, United Kingdom Department of Computing, Imperial College London, United Kingdom. This work focuses on the apparent emotional reaction recognition (AERR) from the video-only input, conducted in a self-supervised fashion. The network is first pre-trained on different self-supervised pretext tasks and later fine-tuned on the downstream target task.

arxiv-2212-08536.title: Detection-aware multi-object tracking evaluation Thanks: This work is part of the preliminary tasks related to the Harvesting Visual Data (HVD) project (PID2021-125051OB-I00) funded by the Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación of the Spanish Government. Thanks: This work was also supported by the H2020
arxiv-2212-08536.creator: Juan C. SanMiguel, Jorge Muñoz, Fabio Poiesi
arxiv-2212-08536.description: Abstract How would you fairly evaluate two multi-object tracking algorithms (i.e. trackers), each one employing a different object detector? Detectors keep improving, thus trackers can make less effort to estimate object states over time. Is it then fair to compare a new tracker employing a new detector with another tracker using an old detector?

arxiv-2311-05898.title: ERNIE: A Reactor Antineutrino Inverse Beta Decay Event Generator Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2311-05898.creator: Murat Altınlı, Halil Gamsızkan
arxiv-2311-05898.description: Abstract We present ERNIE, a computer program which generates nuclear reactor electron antineutrinos and inverse beta decay events induced by these particles, using the Monte-Carlo method. The program allows the usage of different antineutrino energy spectra models and can simulate the time evolution of the overall antineutrino spectrum because of the burn-up effect.

arxiv-2312-14815.title: SuperVortexNet: Reconstructing Superfluid Vortex Filaments Using Deep Learning
arxiv-2312-14815.creator: Nick A. Keepfer, Thomas A. Flynn, Nick G. Parker, Thomas P. Billam
arxiv-2312-14815.description: Abstract We introduce a novel approach to the three-dimensional reconstruction of superfluid vortex filaments using deep convolutional neural networks. Superfluid vortices, quantum mechanical phenomena of immense scientific interest, are challenging to image due to their small dimensions and intricate topology. Here, we propose a deep-learning methodology that serves as a proof-of-principle for fully reconstructing the topology of superfluid vortex filaments.

arxiv-2402-07055.title: Optimization of Super-Directive Linear Arrays with Differential Evolution for High Realized Gain
arxiv-2402-07055.creator: Ihsan Kanbaz 1 2 , Okan Yurduseven 1 , and Michail Matthaiou 1
arxiv-2402-07055.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ihsan Kanbaz 1 2 , Okan Yurduseven 1 , and Michail Matthaiou 1. Due to the low impedance and high feeding currents, it is naturally challenging to design super-directive antenna arrays that perfectly match the feed line, and this becomes almost impossible as the number of elements increases. In this paper, we assert that it is crucial to consider the trade-off between directivity and overall efficiency (to achieve high realized gain) before employing super-directive arrays in real-world applications.

arxiv-2403-00345.title: Microwave-to-optics conversion using magnetostatic modes and a tunable optical cavity
arxiv-2403-00345.creator: Wei-Jiang Wu, Yi-Pu Wang, Jie Li, Gang Li, J. Q. You
arxiv-2403-00345.description: Abstract Quantum computing, quantum communication and quantum networks rely on hybrid quantum systems operating in different frequency ranges. For instance, the superconducting qubits work in the gigahertz range, while the optical photons used in communication are in the range of hundreds of terahertz.

arxiv-2407-05702.title: Modified hybrid inflation in no-scale SUGRA with suppressed R R -symmetry breaking
arxiv-2407-05702.creator: Qian Wan, Da-Xin Zhang
arxiv-2407-05702.description: Abstract A well-motivated cosmological hybrid inflation scenario based on no-scale SUGRA is considered. It is demonstrated that an extra suppressed R R -symmetry breaking term S n S^{n} with n ≥ 4 n\geq 4 needs to be included in order to realize successful inflation.

arxiv-2502-09258.title: A Bayesian estimator for peculiar velocity correction in cosmological inference from supernovae data
arxiv-2502-09258.creator: Ujjwal Upadhyay, Tarun Deep Saini, Shiv K. Sethi
arxiv-2502-09258.description: Abstract The peculiar motion of the host galaxies can shift the observed redshifts from their true values, introducing bias in estimating cosmological parameters from supernova data. The coherent component of peculiar motion is typically corrected using velocity-field reconstruction, while the random component is handled statistically by inflating the magnitude uncertainty through standard error propagation.

arxiv-2503-07723.title: PEPSI Investigation, Retrieval, and Atlas of Numerous Giant Atmospheres (PIRANGA). III. Composition and winds in the atmosphere of TOI-1518 b
arxiv-2503-07723.creator: Connor Basinger, Marshall C. Johnson, Ji Wang, Alison Duck, Anusha Pai Asnodkar, Sydney Petz, Calder Lenhart, Ilya Ilyin, Klaus Strassmeier
arxiv-2503-07723.description: Abstract Ultra-hot Jupiters (UHJs) orbit close to their host stars and experience extreme conditions, making them important laboratories to explore atmospheric composition and dynamics. Transmission spectroscopy is a useful tool to reveal chemical species and their vertical and longitudinal distribution in the atmosphere.

arxiv-2512-03725.title: Probing Azimuthal Alignment in Heavy-Ion Collisions: Clusterization Effects
arxiv-2512-03725.creator: Aleksei Nikolskii, Igor Lokhtin, Alexander Snigirev
arxiv-2512-03725.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aleksei Nikolskii, Igor Lokhtin, Alexander Snigirev. The influence of kinematic constraints and event selection on the emergence of the alignment phenomenon observed in cosmic-ray experiments is studied within the HYDJET++ model. It is demonstrated that the high degree of alignment, previously identified for realistic values of the transverse momentum disbalance of the most energetic particles, is also observed at the level of the most energetic clusters.

arxiv-2602-02357.title: Black Hole Evaporation as a Topological Tunneling
arxiv-2602-02357.creator: Victor H. Alencar
arxiv-2602-02357.description: Abstract We present the quantization of the electromagnetic field near the event horizon of a Schwarzschild black hole using Euclidean path integrals. Our result for the vacuum energy describes a black hole surrounded by a finite volume of photons at T H = 1 8 ​ π ​ G ​ M T_{H}=\frac{1}{8\pi GM} , the black hole quantum atmosphere.

pmc-11654407.title: The influential factors of depression among caregivers of children with Cleft Lip and/or Palate: a path analysis based on diathesis-stress theoretical model
pmc-11654407.creator: Jinrong Yang, Xiaohan Li, Yuqin Gao, Weiren Wang, Junyan Wang, Yanjie Wang, Caixia Gong, Runzi Wang, Lulu Yuan
pmc-11654407.description: BackgroundDepression is the most common psychological phenomenon among caregivers of children with Cleft Lip and/or Palate and affects the quality of life, treatment satisfaction, children’s self-esteem and parent–child relationship. However, Existing studies have limited explanations for the mechanisms that lead to depression in caregivers of children with Cleft Lip and/or Palate.

pmc-12666243.title: A Non‐G‐Quadruplex Hemin Aptamer Forms a Better Peroxidase Mimicking DNAzyme
pmc-12666243.creator: Claudia Rodríguez‐Almazán, Yunus A Kaiyum, Philip E Johnson, Juewen Liu
pmc-12666243.description: G‐quadruplex DNA is known to bind to hemin, forming a complex that exhibits peroxidase‐like activity. A non‐G‐quadruplex aptamer named Hem1‐2T also exhibits horseradish peroxidase (HRP) like activity upon binding to hemin. Herein, the catalytic characteristics of the Hem1‐2T aptamer are studied and compared with PS2.M, an extensively studied G‐quadruplex.

pmc-12735059.title: The Effect of Lipid Extract of Nannochloropsis oceanica Marine Microalgae on Glutathione and Thioredoxin-Dependent Antioxidant Systems in UVB-Irradiated Keratinocytes
pmc-12735059.creator: Agnieszka Gęgotek, Maria Rosario Domingues, Pedro Domingues, Elżbieta Skrzydlewska, Se-Kwon Kim
pmc-12735059.description: UVB radiation present in sunlight is the main pro-oxidative and pro-inflammatory factor that reaches human skin cells, including keratinocytes. Therefore, protective compounds eliminating the negative impact of UVB radiation are constantly being sought. This study aimed to estimate the effect of the lipid extract of microalgae Nannochloropsis oceanica (N.o.) on UVB-irradiated keratinocytes.
